problems.title: apt/dpkg lock held (Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend)
problems.error_text: E: Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend. It is held by process 1234 (unattended-upgr)
problems.context: fresh boot, cloud-init, CI provisioning, Ansible
problems.frequency_signal: one of the most searched Ubuntu errors; many blog posts and Launchpad bugs
root_causes: apt-daily/apt-daily-upgrade timers running unattended-upgrades after boot
fix: wait; apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600
systemd-run --property=After=apt-daily.service ... or systemctl stop apt-daily* in images
never rm lock files; if dpkg interrupted: dpkg --configure -a
problems.prevention: set DPkg::Lock::Timeout in automation; schedule unattended-upgrades windows

learning_signals: Practitioners learn disk/inode/deleted-file problems from their first 3am disk-full page; interview questions reuse them
Netflix 60-second checklist and USE method are the most cited performance starting points
Many fixes in blogs are wrong-layer (limits.conf for systemd services, rm lock files, setenforce 0, chmod 777); the handbook should say what not to do
Ubuntu 22.04-24.04 changed defaults (needrestart interactive, ssh socket activation, apt-key removal, deb822) and community threads spike after each LTS
Postmortems (GitHub 2020 ProxySQL fd cap, Tarsnap 2016 runaway log, 2012 leap second) show host-level limits causing big outages
Lockout recovery depends on out-of-band access: IPMI/iDRAC/hypervisor console on-prem, serial console/SSM in cloud
